DrivAerML test cars are the real test. They are held out from training and have a high-fidelity (hybrid RANS-LES) answer on the same mesh, so the error numbers are meaningful.

The production cars are outside what these models learned. Both models were trained only on 400-odd morphs of one car, the DrivAer (an Audi A4 / BMW 3 Series blend). A Model X or a Taycan is a different shape, so a large error there says the model does not generalise, not that the car's drag is wrong.

The fan meshes are not wind-tunnel geometry. They have a smoothed underbody, closed grilles and simplified wheels, and we scaled each to the published length. Each was shrink-wrapped into one watertight outer skin before inference (the raw meshes had zero-area faces, interior shells and some were upside down). Published drag values come from different tunnels and conditions (see table sources).

The controls test the wrap, not the car. Three DrivAerML cars went through the same shrink-wrap, with the CFD answer carried over. If the models stay accurate on those, the wrap is not what moves the production-car numbers.
